## Prep work

- **tidyverse** packages: https://www.tidyverse.org/packages/

- Powerful and popular for working with complicated dataset, typically formatted into a **tidy** format


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(Lock5Data)
```
:::



- We'll use the **HollywoodMovies** dataset

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
str(HollywoodMovies)
head(HollywoodMovies)
?HollywoodMovies
```
:::



## Review questions
- How many genres are there?  How many movies are in each genre?
\vspace{10pt}
- What are the 10 movies with largest difference (in absolute value) between RottenTomatoes and AudienceScore?
\vspace{10pt}
- Compare the mean AudienceScore by Genre of the movies.
\vspace{10pt}
- What are the top 5 highest WorldGross action movies?
\vspace{10pt}
- What is the highest WorldGross movie for each of the genre?
\vspace{40pt}



## Subsetting: **'['**
The square bracket syntax can be used as a function, with the function name **'['**

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
HollywoodMovies$Movie[1:5]
'['(HollywoodMovies$Movie, 1:5)  # as a function
HollywoodMovies$Movie %>% '['(1:5) # pipe version

HollywoodMovies[5,1]
HollywoodMovies %>% '['(5,1)

HollywoodMovies[5,]
HollywoodMovies %>% '['(5,)
```
:::





## Subsetting: **filter**
\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Get info of action movies
HollywoodMovies[HollywoodMovies$Genre=='Action',]
subset(HollywoodMovies, Genre=='Action')
filter(HollywoodMovies, Genre=='Action')

# filter is easier with multiple conditions
filter(HollywoodMovies, Genre=='Action', Profitability>500)

# pipe version
HollywoodMovies %>% filter(Genre=='Action', Profitability>500)
```
:::


\normalsize
(You can check which package a function belongs to on the help page. Try **?subset** and **?filter**.)


## Subsetting: **slice** and **select**

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# returns user-specified rows
HollywoodMovies %>% slice(c(1,3,5))

# returns user-specified variables
HollywoodMovies %>% select(Movie, Genre)
HollywoodMovies %>% 
  select(-LeadStudio,-TheatersOpenWeek, -RottenTomatoes)
```
:::


\normalsize
Recall, you can use these functions in the regular, none-pipe way:

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
slice(HollywoodMovies, c(1,3,5))
select(HollywoodMovies, Movie, Genre)
```
:::


## Sampling: **sample_frac** and **sample_n**

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# returns a fraction of randomly sampled data
HollywoodMovies %>% sample_frac(0.1)
HollywoodMovies %>% sample_frac(0.1,replace=T)

#returns a few randomly sampled rows
HollywoodMovies %>% sample_n(5)
```
:::



## Sorting: **arrange** and **top_n**

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# arrange ascendingly by WorldGross
HollywoodMovies %>% 
        arrange(WorldGross) %>%
        slice(1:5)

# arrange descendingly
HollywoodMovies %>% 
        arrange(desc(WorldGross)) %>%
        slice(1:5) %>%
        select(Movie, Genre,WorldGross)

# top three movies in terms of WorldGross (but not ordered)
HollywoodMovies %>% top_n(3, WorldGross)
```
:::



## Grouping: **group_by** and **ungroup**

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# group by Genre
HollywoodMovies %>% 
  group_by(Genre) %>%
  summarise(mean(WorldGross))

# review: can also use tapply
tapply(HollywoodMovies$WorldGross, HollywoodMovies$Genre, mean)

# group by Genre + Year
HollywoodMovies %>% 
  group_by(Genre, Year) %>%
  summarise(mean_WorldGross=mean(WorldGross),count=length(WorldGross))
```
:::



## Example: top 5 most profitable genres

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
HollywoodMovies %>%
  filter(!is.na(Profitability)) %>%
  group_by(Genre) %>%
  summarise(meanProfit=mean(Profitability),
            numMovie=length(Profitability)) %>%
  arrange(desc(meanProfit)) %>%
  slice(1:5)
```
:::


\normalsize
- Nothing is stored; no change is made in the data frame.


## Creating new variables

\footnotesize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# new variable not stored, but can be used as part of the pipe operator
HollywoodMovies %>% 
  mutate(RottenAudience = RottenTomatoes + AudienceScore) %>%
  top_n(5, RottenAudience) %>%
  select(Movie, RottenTomatoes, AudienceScore, RottenAudience)

# to store the new variable
HollywoodMovies = HollywoodMovies %>% 
  mutate(RottenAudience = RottenTomatoes + AudienceScore)

# to keep some variables but drop everything else
# (equivalently: mutate and select)
HollywoodMovies %>% 
  transmute(Movie, RottenAudience = RottenTomatoes + AudienceScore)

# to rename variables
HollywoodMovies %>% 
  rename(OpenWeekendGross=OpeningWeekend, 
         OpenWeekendAvg=BOAvgOpenWeekend)

rm(HollywoodMovies)
```
:::




## tibble
A tibble (**tbl**) is an "enhanced" version of a data frame (see https://tibble.tidyverse.org/).  It can be more flexible (e.g.: a variable doesn't have to be a vector) and works better with factors (e.g.: no automatic factor-character type change).  Can handle more complicated dataset (e.g.: time-series):

- day 1: df.patient with 100 patients and 10 variables
- day 2: df.patient with 100 patients and 10 variables...

You can convert HollywoodMovies to a tibble format; all of the previous data manipulation functions would still work.

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tbl_movie <- tibble::as_tibble(HollywoodMovies)
class(tbl_movie)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"
```


:::
:::


tibbles also print better. Try printing `tbl_movie` and compare it with `HollywoodMovies`.


# Sample code for the warn up questions

##
\scriptsize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# How many genres are there?  How many movies are in each genre?
HollywoodMovies %>%
      count(Genre, name = "number of movies")
```
:::


\scriptsize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# What are the 10 movies with largest diff b/t RottenTomatoes & AudienceScore?
HollywoodMovies %>%
        mutate(diff = RottenTomatoes - AudienceScore) %>%
        top_n(10, abs(diff)) %>%
        select(Movie, RottenTomatoes, AudienceScore, diff)
```
:::


\scriptsize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Compare the mean AudienceScore by Genre of the movies.
HollywoodMovies %>%
        group_by(Genre) %>%
        summarize(AudienceScore_mean=mean(AudienceScore, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        arrange(desc(AudienceScore_mean))
```
:::


##
\scriptsize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# What are the top 5 highest WorldGross action movies?
HollywoodMovies %>%
        filter(Genre == "Action") %>%
        arrange(desc(WorldGross)) %>%
        slice(1:5) %>%
        select(Movie, Genre,WorldGross)
```
:::


\scriptsize

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# What is the highest WorldGross movie for each of the genre?
HollywoodMovies %>%
        group_by(Genre) %>%
        top_n(1, WorldGross) %>%
        select(Movie, Genre,WorldGross)
```
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
